proposals.rationale: appdirs was abandoned in 2017 with known path resolution bugs on Windows and macOS. 'platformdirs' is the officially endorsed, actively maintained community fork with 100% backward-compatible API for user_cache_dir().
migration_steps: Change 'from appdirs import user_cache_dir' to 'from platformdirs import user_cache_dir' in linkwatch/cache.py
Replace 'appdirs==1.4.4' with 'platformdirs>=3.0.0' in requirements.txt and pyproject.toml

+++ b/LinkWatch/linkwatch/cache.py
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@

 import os
 
-from appdirs import user_cache_dir
+from platformdirs import user_cache_dir
 
 RESULTS_FILE = "results.json"
 
--- a/LinkWatch/requirements.txt
+++ b/LinkWatch/requirements.txt
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
 toml==0.10.2
-appdirs==1.4.4
+platformdirs>=3.0.0

-    "appdirs==1.4.4",

verification_tests:
def test_platformdirs_user_cache_dir():
    from linkwatch.cache import cache_dir
    path = cache_dir()
    assert os.path.exists(path)
    assert 'linkwatch' in path.lower()
compatibility_gaps_and_limitations: platformdirs adheres to modern XDG and OS standards. Cache directory paths on some Linux distributions may place cache under ~/.cache/linkwatch/ rather than ~/.cache/linkwatch.

proposals.rationale: 'idna==2.7' is an ancient 2018 pin pinned directly in root manifests without being imported directly in LinkWatch. It artificially restricts transitive resolution of modern requests/urllib3 stacks.
migration_steps: Remove direct pin 'idna==2.7' from requirements.txt

proposals.rationale: Jinja2==2.11.3 (2021) is broken under modern environments because it imports 'soft_unicode' from markupsafe, which MarkupSafe 3.0 removed. This caused the verified baseline test failure in test_report.py. Bumping to Jinja2>=3.1.5 restores compatibility and patches security advisories.
migration_steps: Update requirements.txt: change Jinja2==2.11.3 to Jinja2>=3.1.5
Update pyproject.toml: change Jinja2==2.11.3 to Jinja2>=3.1.5
Re-run test_report.py to verify HTML report rendering passes without markupsafe errors

verification_tests:
def test_jinja2_report_rendering(tmp_path):
    from linkwatch.report import render_report
    out = tmp_path / 'out.html'
    render_report([{'name': 'Test', 'url': 'http://test', 'up': True}], output=str(out))
    assert out.exists()
    assert 'Test' in out.read_text()
compatibility_gaps_and_limitations: Jinja2 3.x dropped Python 2/3.5 support and deprecated older extension hooks, none of which are used in LinkWatch's single HTML template.

proposals.rationale: 'nose' was abandoned in 2015 and relies on standard library 'imp', which was removed in Python 3.12 (PEP 594). All LinkWatch tests are already written for pytest.
migration_steps: Remove 'nose==1.3.7' from requirements-dev.txt
Remove 'test-nose' target and nosetests references from Makefile
Retain pytest as the sole standard test runner

proposals.rationale: Manifest conflict: requirements.txt pins 'pydantic==1.10.13', whereas pyproject.toml declares 'pydantic>=2'. The codebase uses Pydantic v1 syntax (@validator, class Config). Resolution requires harmonizing manifest versions and updating models to v2 syntax (field_validator, ConfigDict) or pydantic.v1 compatibility shim.
migration_steps: Harmonize manifests by standardizing on pydantic>=2 in both requirements.txt and pyproject.toml
Update linkwatch/config.py to use pydantic v2 @field_validator and ConfigDict (or pydantic.v1 import shim for transitional stability)

verification_tests:
def test_pydantic_site_validation():
    from linkwatch.config import Site
    import pytest
    s = Site(name='Test', url='https://test.com')
    assert s.name == 'Test'
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Site(name='', url='https://test.com')
compatibility_gaps_and_limitations: Pydantic v2 has slight changes in error dictionary structure and validation error message formatting. Any tests checking exact regex match on ValidationError strings may need adjustment.

proposals.rationale: linkwatch/resources.py uses deprecated 'pkg_resources' to locate package templates. Python 3.9+ provides 'importlib.resources.files' natively, eliminating the runtime setuptools dependency entirely.
migration_steps: Refactor linkwatch/resources.py to use standard library 'importlib.resources.files'
Remove 'setuptools==75.8.0' from runtime requirements.txt (retain in build-system of pyproject.toml only)

proposals.rationale: The external 'toml' package is unmaintained since 2020. Python 3.11+ natively provides 'tomllib' in the standard library. Note: tomllib.load requires opening files in binary mode ('rb').
migration_steps: Replace 'import toml' with 'import sys; import tomllib if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else ...' in linkwatch/config.py
Update load_settings() in linkwatch/config.py to open files in binary read mode ('rb')
Remove 'toml==0.10.2' from requirements.txt and pyproject.toml dependencies
proposals.unified_diff:
--- a/LinkWatch/linkwatch/config.py
+++ b/LinkWatch/linkwatch/config.py
@@ -1,6 +1,10 @@
 from typing import List
 
-import toml
+import sys
+if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
+    import tomllib
+else:
+    import tomli as tomllib
 from pydantic import BaseModel, validator
 
 
@@ -34,5 +38,6 @@
 
 
 def load_settings(path="sites.toml"):
-    data = toml.load(path)
+    with open(path, "rb") as f:
+        data = tomllib.load(f)
     return Settings(**data)
verification_tests:
def test_load_settings_with_tomllib(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / 'sites.toml'
    p.write_text('title = "test"\n[[sites]]\nname = "Example"\nurl = "https://example.com"\n')
    cfg = load_settings(str(p))
    assert cfg.title == 'test'
    assert len(cfg.sites) == 1
compatibility_gaps_and_limitations: tomllib only parses TOML (read-only). If writing/dumping TOML is ever needed, tomli-w or tomlkit would be required (LinkWatch is read-only for sites.toml).
